scenarios.input: The plan is done. Implement milestone 1: add the retry loop to the uploader with its regression test. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented trigger `implement this slice` in substance and follows a plan. A response that assigns a complexity tier, runs a pre-mortem before code, and writes the failing test before the implementation is attributable to this skill rather than to generic coding help.

scenarios.desc: A new detector must be self-applied before it is committed
scenarios.input: Add a pre-push linter that flags any function over 80 lines, plus a unit test for it against a fixture. The fixture test passes, so we are done. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. A fixture test proves the detector's logic and proves nothing about its threshold, so a generic responder accepts the claim of done. Step 6 requires running the new detector against the current branch and confirming it fires on conditions already present. A response that demands that run before the commit is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Reviewing a finished diff is not building
scenarios.input: Read the diff on this branch and tell me whether the architecture is sound. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for review of finished work, which the skill's description routes elsewhere. It names no slice, no plan step, and no implementation trigger, so build should stay inactive.

scenarios.desc: A validator fix must clear the provenance/authority gate before editing
scenarios.input: The Gate 3 validator at scripts/validation/check_secrets.py flags a false positive on a test fixture. Fix the validator's regex and add a regression test. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The path scripts/validation/check_secrets.py matches the validator-code path cue (issue #5387), so a response attributable to this skill runs Phase 2b before touching the file: classify provenance, get authorization, and name the one permitted change location. A generic responder edits the regex directly with no ownership check.

scenarios.desc: An unrelated feature change skips the provenance/authority gate
scenarios.input: Implement milestone 2: add pagination to the /orders list endpoint in src/api/orders.py, with its regression test. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: src/api/orders.py matches no validator path cue and carries no validation-semantics effect, so Phase 2b's trigger should report skip with a stated reason and the response moves straight to Phase 3, still showing the ordinary tier, pre-mortem, and atomic-commit signals without inventing a provenance record for an unrelated file.

scenarios.desc: A code-only diff that changes a documented count saves a doc-impact record
scenarios.input: My diff only changes src/filters.py: the registry now holds 4 filters, and docs/guide.md still says 'the three filters'. Implement the slice and tell me what you carry to /test. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: No Markdown file changed, so an extension test records no documentation impact and the stale count escapes. Exit gate 3 passes the verified quantitative-claim effect to doc_accuracy_trigger.py, saves the JSON as the doc-impact record, and hands its path to /test Gate 5. Naming the trigger and the record is attributable to the skill rather than to a generic reminder to update the docs.

scenarios.desc: A tests-only slice records an explicit documentation skip instead of a full audit
scenarios.input: My slice only adds tests/test_uploader.py for the retry loop. Implement it and tell me what you do about documentation. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A test file cannot invalidate a durable claim, so the trigger decides skip and exit gate 3 records DOC ACCURACY: SKIPPED with the reason. A generic responder either runs a full documentation audit or says nothing; quoting the trigger's skip reason is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: An in-scope gate regression is repaired and revalidated
scenarios.input: Work order allows only src/uploader/ and tests/uploader/. Exit gate 1 flags a regression in src/uploader/retry.py that my diff introduced. What do you do? Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The finding is caused by the diff and sits inside the allowed paths, so the Gate failure disposition table says repair in this cycle and rerun the gate. A generic responder defers it to review, which the skill rejects.

scenarios.desc: Unrelated drift fails a required gate outside the allowed paths
scenarios.input: Work order allows only src/uploader/. Exit gate 4 (orphan-ref-validator) returns CRITICAL_FAIL on docs/old-guide.md, which this diff never touched. A teammate says to fix that file in this PR so the gate is green. What do you do? Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Out-of-scope drift on a required gate is a Blocker: no edit outside the allowed paths, the gate stays FAILED, the finding is recorded in the handoff, and the branch stops with the owner named. Fixing the file or marking the gate passed are the failure modes.

scenarios.desc: Recorded blocker evidence changed on a repeated run
scenarios.input: Last run I recorded gate 4 failing on docs/old-guide.md at head abc123 as out of scope. The branch now has new commits and gate 4 also fails on src/uploader/README.md, inside the allowed paths. What do you do? Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Recorded evidence is reused only after a freshness check on head SHA and failing paths. The new failure is inside the allowed paths, so it is reclassified in scope and repaired, while the old finding is rechecked rather than trusted.
